extraction.Name: Pearl Twiss, nee Janis
extraction.Refused/Protested: did not wish her patent in fee to her 160 acre allotment, when it was issued, September 29, 1919, but the Indian Agency told her that it would be assessed for the taxes, and later sold for same, if she did not accept the patent, and pay her taxes, so she accepted it
extraction.Sold/Mortgaged: about two months after she received the patent in fee, she sold her allotment to her brother, James Janis, for $1200.00 cash
extraction.Tax burden forced sale/Mortgage: did not sell her land for debts incurred prior to receiving her patent in fee
extraction.Occupation/Income: does domestic work for her living; and that is her only source of income
extraction.NOTES: Mentally competent; good health; separated from her husband; has one minor child to support, the father not helping toward the support of the child; child has good health; considers she received a good price for her land; has never received any help from the County, State nor the United States Government; document signed before notary public December 26, 1928
